mainTopic: Who inherits when relatives die together and no one knows who died first (husband and wife, then son and mother), followed by a puzzling ruling from ארץ ישראל about a son and his father's property.
overview: The גמרא first asks whose ownership בית הלל meant when they said the wife's guaranteed property stays 'בחזקתן'. רבי יוחנן says the husband's heirs, and רבי אלעזר says the wife's heirs. ריש לקיש, in the name of בר קפרא, says they split it, and a ברייתא of בר קפרא backs this up. A new משנה deals with a house that fell on a son and his mother: both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the heirs split, but רבי עקיבא says the property stays in its ownership. בן עזאי protests that רבי עקיבא is creating a dispute where there was none. The גמרא asks whose ownership רבי עקיבא means. רבי אילא says the mother's heirs and רבי זירא says the son's heirs. After moving to ארץ ישראל, רבי זירא switched to רבי אילא's view and concluded that the air of ארץ ישראל makes one wise. אביי explains that the property stays with the mother's heirs because it was already established in her tribe. רבי שמלאי learns from בן עזאי's direct 'you came' that he was a תלמיד חבר of רבי עקיבא. Finally, a puzzling ruling arrives from ארץ ישראל about a son who 'borrowed' on his father's property. The גמרא shows that its wording cannot be right and begins to reword it, and the corrected wording comes on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Whose possession does the wife's property stay in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בית הלל meant when they said the wife's guaranteed property stays 'in its ownership'. Whose ownership?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: In whose possession does it stay?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking a clarifying question about the earlier משנה. It is setting up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, a house fell on a husband and wife and no one knows who died first. בית הלל said the property stays 'בחזקתן', in its current ownership. For the guaranteed property the wife brought into the marriage, it is not obvious whose 'current ownership' that is, because the wife owns it but the husband is responsible for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
In the possession or presumed ownership of
Presumed status: we leave things where they are until proven otherwise

phrases.english: גמרא: In whose possession?
phrases.notes: This goes back to בית הלל's words in the earlier משנה, that the property stays 'in its ownership'.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side's heirs count as the current owners of the wife's guaranteed property: the husband's or the wife's?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the husband's heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the property stays with the husband's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: in the possession of the husband's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer: the husband's heirs keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband was the one responsible for this property and had to pay his wife back if it was lost. So רבי יוחנן treats it as already in his side's possession, and his heirs keep it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּחֶזְקַת יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: in the possession of the husband's heirs,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The property stays with the husband's heirs.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the wife's heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר disagrees and says the property stays with the wife's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר says: in the possession of the wife's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the opposite answer: the wife's heirs keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This property came from the wife's father's house, so at its root it belongs to her. For רבי אלעזר that makes her family the current owners.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: בְּחֶזְקַת יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says: in the possession of the wife's heirs,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רבי יוחנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The property stays with the wife's heirs.

steps.title: ריש לקיש in the name of בר קפרא: they split it
steps.stepSummary: A third opinion: neither side keeps all of it. They divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש says in the name of בר קפרא: they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view says neither side wins outright, so the two sides split the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר each pick one side as the clear owner. This view says neither side clearly owns it, so the fair outcome is to divide it.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says in the name of bar Kappara:
They divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A middle position between the two previous opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two sides split the property.

steps.title: בר קפרא's ברייתא supports splitting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא taught by בר קפרא backs up the ruling to split, and gives the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too בר קפרא teaches: since these come to inherit and those come to inherit, they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that בר קפרא also taught this ruling in a ברייתא, which supports ריש לקיש's report and gives the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that both sides come as heirs, and neither side can prove its claim. Since they stand equally, they split.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the wife's guaranteed property: the husband's heirs (רבי יוחנן), the wife's heirs (רבי אלעזר), or split it (בר קפרא). Splitting is justified because both sides are equally heirs.

phrases.english: And so too bar Kappara teaches:
Since these come to inherit
and those come to inherit, they divide it.

steps.raayaObject: The ruling of ריש לקיש in the name of בר קפרא that they split
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by בר קפרא himself

steps.title: New משנה: a house falls on a son and his mother
steps.stepSummary: If a house falls on a son and his mother and no one knows who died first, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the heirs split the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the house fell on him and on his mother, both these and those agree that they divide.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה brings a new case, a son and his mother killed together, and says that here everyone agrees to split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's father's family says the son died first, so they inherit the mother. The son's heirs say the mother died first, so the son inherited her and they inherit him. In the husband-and-wife case בית שמאי and בית הלל argued, but here 'these and those', both schools, agree to divide.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those: here, both בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.confusionAlert: עָלָיו here means the son, not the husband. The case is a son and his mother, so the two sides are the mother's father's family and the son's heirs.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ נָפַל הַבַּיִת עָלָיו וְעַל אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: משנה: If the house collapsed on him and on his mother,
both these and those agree that they divide it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the son-and-mother case, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the property is split.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: here the property stays in its ownership
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that in this case he holds the property stays where it is. It is not split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I agree in this case that the property stays in its ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the 'everyone agrees to split' ruling and says the property stays in its current ownership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא uses בית הלל's own phrase from the earlier case, 'בחזקתן', and applies it here as well. He does not say whose ownership he means. The גמרא asks that question in step 9.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
I agree in this case that the property stays in its ownership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מוֹדֶה אֲנִי בָּזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first ruling of the משנה, that both schools agree to split.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the son-and-mother case the property stays in its current ownership.

steps.title: בן עזאי objects to creating a new argument
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי complains that רבי עקיבא is making a dispute where בית שמאי and בית הלל agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to him: We are already pained over the cases they argue about. Are you now coming to create an argument in a case where they agree?!
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי pushes back sharply against רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Disputes between בית שמאי and בית הלל already trouble the חכמים. Here both schools agreed to split. By ruling otherwise, רבי עקיבא would add a new disagreement where there was none.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who disagree / cases of dispute
Those who are equal, meaning in agreement

steps.whatToRemember: In the son-and-mother case, both schools say split. רבי עקיבא says the property stays in its ownership, and בן עזאי protests that he is creating a new dispute.

phrases.english: Ben Azzai said to him:
We are pained over the cases where they disagree;
phrases.notes: The letter ה in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, so read it as 'the' disagreements.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁבָּאתָ לְחַלֵּק עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַשָּׁוִין?!
phrases.english: and now you come to bring a disagreement upon us in a case where they agree?!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that the property stays in its ownership
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both בית שמאי and בית הלל agreed to split, so ruling otherwise creates a new and unwanted dispute.

steps.title: Whose ownership does רבי עקיבא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose possession the property stays in according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: In whose possession?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked before, now about רבי עקיבא's words in this משנה. It is setting up two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said 'בחזקתן' but did not say whose ownership. The property could be seen as belonging to the mother's side or to the son's side.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same wording as step 1, but it is a new question. Step 1 asked about בית הלל in the husband-and-wife case. This one asks about רבי עקיבא in the son-and-mother case.

phrases.english: גמרא: In whose possession?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי עקיבא, do the mother's heirs or the son's heirs count as current owners?

steps.title: רבי אילא: the mother's heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא says the property stays with the mother's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא says: in the possession of the mother's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילא answers that the mother's family keeps the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The property was the mother's to begin with. Since no one can prove the son ever inherited it, it stays with her family.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אִילָא אָמַר: בְּחֶזְקַת יוֹרְשֵׁי הָאֵם.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ila says: in the possession of the mother's heirs.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The property stays with the mother's heirs.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the son's heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, while still in בבל, says the property stays with the son's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא says: in the possession of the son's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives the opposite answer: the son's heirs keep the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא reads רבי עקיבא's 'בחזקתן' as pointing to the son's side, the opposite of רבי אילא. The גמרא gives no reason for this view, and the next step shows he later changed his mind.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר: בְּחֶזְקַת יוֹרְשֵׁי הַבֵּן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says: in the possession of the son's heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רבי אילא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The property stays with the son's heirs.

steps.title: רבי זירא switches sides, and רבה takes his old view
steps.stepSummary: After moving to ארץ ישראל, רבי זירא adopted רבי אילא's view, while רבה in בבל adopted רבי זירא's old view.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he took up the view of רבי אילא. רבה took up the view of רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells what happened next: רבי זירא changed his opinion after moving, and רבה in בבל held on to רבי זירא's original opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions effectively traded places. The view of ארץ ישראל (mother's heirs) won over רבי זירא once he arrived there. The view he left behind in בבל (son's heirs) was carried on by רבה. This sets up רבי זירא's comment in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up (moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל)
Took up his view / adopted his position

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
phrases.notes: Went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he took up the view of Rabbi Ila.
Rabba took up the view of Rabbi Zeira.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how the two opinions of steps 10 and 11 shifted between the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא retracted and agreed with רבי אילא (mother's heirs), while רבה held the son's heirs view.

steps.title: The air of ארץ ישראל makes one wise
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא concludes from his own change of mind that the air of ארץ ישראל makes a person wise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Learn from this that the air of ארץ ישראל makes one wise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a lesson from what happened: living in ארץ ישראל brought him to the wiser view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he was in ארץ ישראל, he saw that רבי אילא's view was correct. רבה, who stayed in בבל, still held the view רבי זירא had dropped. רבי זירא credits the land itself with this added wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / conclude from this

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, the son-and-mother property stays with the mother's heirs. That is רבי אילא's view, which רבי זירא accepted in ארץ ישראל, while רבה held the son's heirs view. רבי זירא's famous line: the air of ארץ ישראל makes one wise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the well-known saying 'אוירא דארץ ישראל מחכים', about the special wisdom of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Learn from this
that the air of Eretz Yisrael makes one wise.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's switch to רבי אילא's view (mother's heirs) after moving shows that the air of ארץ ישראל makes one wise.

steps.title: Why does the property stay with the mother's heirs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אילא's answer that, according to רבי עקיבא, the property stays with the mother's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now knows the final answer: the property stays with the mother's heirs. It asks why, and this sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 settled who keeps the property, but not the reason. The mother's heirs and the son's heirs could each claim it, so the גמרא wants to know what tips the balance toward the mother's side.

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the view that step 13 accepted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the property stays with the mother's heirs according to רבי עקיבא

steps.title: אביי: the inheritance was already settled in that tribe
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the property was already established in the mother's tribe, so we do not take it out of that tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because the inheritance was already established in that tribe.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The property was already held by the mother's family and tribe, so it stays there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before anything happened, the property belonged to the mother. Giving it to the son's heirs would move it from her tribe to a different tribe. Since we cannot know who died first, we leave the property where it was already firmly placed.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, the property stays with the mother's heirs. The reason is that it was already established in her tribe, and we do not move it out on a doubt.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Since the inheritance was established in that tribe.
phrases.notes: "That tribe" means the mother's tribe, the family the property came from.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הוֹאִיל וְהוּחְזְקָה נַחֲלָה בְּאוֹתוֹ שֵׁבֶט
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The property was already established in the mother's tribe, so it stays with her heirs and is not moved to another tribe

steps.title: Quoting בן עזאי's protest from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה where בן עזאי protests to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to him: We are already troubled over the cases where they disagree, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes בן עזאי's reply to רבי עקיבא. This quote sets up the comment of רבי שמלאי in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי and בית הלל agreed about this case, and רבי עקיבא came with a different view. בן עזאי complains that their disputes are already hard enough, and now רבי עקיבא creates a dispute even where they agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Ben Azzai said to him:
We are troubled over those who disagree, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: "and you come to make a dispute where they agree?" The word that matters next is "you come," שבאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עַזַּאי: עַל הַחֲלוּקִין אָנוּ מִצְטַעֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה to discuss its next line
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי protests that רבי עקיבא is creating a dispute where בית שמאי and בית הלל agreed

steps.title: בן עזאי was a student-colleague of רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי learns from בן עזאי's direct wording that he was a תלמיד חבר of רבי עקיבא, not only a student.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי said: This tells us that בן עזאי was a student-colleague of רבי עקיבא, since he said to him "you came."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי notices how בן עזאי spoke to רבי עקיבא. From that, he learns what kind of relationship the two had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי addressed רבי עקיבא as "you," saying "שבאת" ("you came"). A plain student would speak to his rebbe in a more formal, indirect way, not as "you." This shows that בן עזאי was a תלמיד חבר: someone who learned from רבי עקיבא but stood close to him as a colleague.

keyTerms.meaning: A student who is also a colleague

phrases.english: Rabbi Simlai said,
This tells us

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן עַזַּאי תַּלְמִיד חָבֵר דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: that Ben Azzai was a student-colleague of Rabbi Akiva,
since he said to him "you came."
phrases.notes: Talking to him as "you" this directly is how you speak to a peer, not how a plain student speaks to his rebbe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the wording quoted in step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי was a תלמיד חבר of רבי עקיבא, as shown by his direct address "you came"

steps.title: A ruling from ארץ ישראל about a son who borrowed on his father's property
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis of ארץ ישראל sent a ruling: a son who borrowed on his father's property while the father was alive, and then the father died, can take the property back from the buyers. They called this the hardest ruling in monetary law.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: A son who borrowed on his father's property during his father's lifetime, and then the father died, his son takes it back from the buyers. And this is the hardest ruling in monetary law.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ruling arrives from ארץ ישראל, and it even comes labeled as very hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case involves a son who dealt with his father's property before he inherited it. After the father died, the property may be taken back from the people who got it. The senders themselves warn that this ruling is the hardest one in דיני ממונות.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, from ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try too hard to make sense of the word "borrowed" here. The very next step shows that the גמרא itself finds this wording impossible as written.

phrases.english: They sent from there:
A son who borrowed on his father's property
during his father's lifetime, and he died —
phrases.notes: The one who died is the father.

phrases.english: his son takes it out of the hands of the buyers.
And this is the one that is difficult in monetary law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the case of the mother and son
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son who 'borrowed' on his father's property during the father's life, and then the father died, takes it back from the buyers. This is called the hardest ruling in monetary law.

steps.title: The wording makes no sense: borrowing and buyers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ruling. A borrower has to pay, so what could he take back? And the ruling never mentioned any buyers, so where do they come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he borrowed, what is he taking out? And also, what do buyers have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling as it was sent. It points out two problems that show the wording cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First problem: someone who borrows owes money, so it makes no sense that he would "take out" anything. Second problem: the case only spoke about borrowing, yet the ruling suddenly mentions buyers that were never brought in.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they have to do with it?

phrases.english: He borrowed — what is he taking out?
And furthermore, what do buyers have to do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָוָה מַאי מַפֵּיק? וְעוֹד, לָקוֹחוֹת מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ruling from step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording "borrowed" and the mention of "buyers" in the ruling from ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A borrower owes money and has nothing to collect. Also, no buyers appear in the case, so the ruling does not fit together.

steps.title: The גמרא begins to reword the ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to explain how the ruling must really have been said. The full rewording comes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, it was said like this —
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is about to give a corrected version of the ruling that answers both problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "rather, if it was said" admit that the original wording cannot stand. They promise a new version of the case that will explain both what the son takes back and who the buyers are.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, it was like this —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the challenge of step 19 by rewording the ruling
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the ruling as it was sent

steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling must have been said differently; the corrected wording follows
